blocks.text: 1. Subword Tokenization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446160194-774507248.png

Tokenization's own closing recap, already covered in Tokenization, pointed forward here. Subword Tokenization, a scheme sitting between whole words and individual characters, is the practical solution used by nearly every modern language model.
It genuinely splits rare words into smaller, reusable pieces while keeping common words whole, a balance explored in full throughout this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to Tokenization's own closing recap, already covered in Tokenization. Subword tokenization was genuinely previewed there as sitting between word and character level splitting, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely gives it the complete, dedicated treatment already promised, exploring every detail already hinted at generally in that earlier topic.
3. Recapping The Two Extremes
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446160194-800466845.png

This connects back to word level and character level splitting, both already covered in Tokenization. Word level splitting genuinely gives a huge vocabulary; character level splitting genuinely gives very long sequences.
Subword tokenization genuinely aims for a genuinely practical middle ground between those two extremes, the core idea explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Splitting Rare Words Into Pieces
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446160194-493815238.png
This connects back to the two extremes, already covered in this topic. Genuinely common words genuinely stay as one single whole token.
Genuinely rare or unseen words genuinely get broken down into smaller, already-known subword pieces instead, the genuinely core mechanism explored throughout the rest of this topic.
5. Byte Pair Encoding
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446160195-824162528.png

This connects back to splitting rare words into pieces, already covered in this topic. Byte Pair Encoding genuinely builds its vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent pair of symbols.
Starting from genuinely individual characters and genuinely growing outward into common subword chunks, a genuinely widely used, concrete algorithm explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This merging process, already covered in this topic, directly explains why Byte Pair Encoding vocabularies naturally include both common whole words and smaller, reusable subword fragments.

blocks.text: 6. WordPiece Tokenization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446160195-587331918.png

This connects back to Byte Pair Encoding, already covered in this topic. WordPiece, a genuinely related scheme, genuinely chooses merges that maximize training data likelihood instead of raw frequency.
This genuinely produces a similar style of subword vocabulary through a genuinely different selection criterion, a genuinely useful variant explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 7. Handling Unseen Words Gracefully
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446160420-320873509.png
This connects back to splitting rare words into pieces, already covered in this topic. An entirely unseen word genuinely still breaks down into already-known subword pieces.

This genuinely avoids the unknown-word problem already covered as word level splitting's own limitation in Tokenization, a genuinely real practical advantage explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This graceful handling, already covered in this topic, directly explains why subword tokenization has become the genuinely dominant choice behind nearly every modern large language model, already covered generally elsewhere in this module.

blocks.text: 8. Vocabulary Size Tradeoff
This connects back to handling unseen words gracefully, already covered in this topic. A genuinely larger subword vocabulary genuinely keeps more whole words intact, shortening sequences.

A genuinely smaller vocabulary genuinely forces more splitting, lengthening sequences but shrinking the vocabulary itself, a genuinely real, tunable tradeoff explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Subword tokenization sits between whole word and individual character level splitting.
Common words stay as one single whole token; rare or unseen words get broken into smaller pieces.
Byte Pair Encoding builds its vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent symbol pair.
WordPiece is a related scheme, choosing merges by training data likelihood instead of raw frequency.
Unseen words still break down into already-known subword pieces, avoiding the unknown-word problem.
A larger vocabulary keeps more words intact and shortens sequences; a smaller one does the opposite.
This balance makes subword tokenization the dominant choice behind nearly every modern language model.
